fields_added_by_the_completeness_critic.brief: Modern stochastic thermodynamics of computation, the precise version of 'entropy relative to what the system knows' and of what locality costs in heat. Seminal sources: Parrondo, Horowitz, Sagawa 'Thermodynamics of information' (Nature Physics 2015); Sagawa 'Thermodynamic and logical reversibilities revisited' (J. Stat. Mech. 2014), on logically irreversible steps that can still be run thermodynamically reversibly; Kolchinsky and Wolpert 'Dependence of dissipation on the initial distribution over states' (2017), on mismatch cost, the extra heat a device pays when its built-in prior differs from its real inputs; Wolpert 'The stochastic thermodynamics of computation' (J. Phys. A 2019); Wolpert and Kolchinsky 'Thermodynamics of computing with circuits' (NJP 2020); Boyd, Mandal, Crutchfield 'Thermodynamics of modularity: structural costs beyond the Landauer bound' (PRX 2018), on local gates paying extra because they cannot see global correlations; and the information-ratchet line (Mandal and Jarzynski PNAS 2012; Boyd, Mandal, Crutchfield 'Correlation-powered information engines' PRE 2017), where a local machine reads a tape and spends that tape's correlations or blankness as fuel. Focus: whether a K drop or triage drop costs heat depends on the distribution, not just on whether the step is many-to-one. How much heat 2x2x2-local rules must lose compared with a global optimum, and so how much locality costs. Whether a stored history tape can be fuel that a later local ratchet uses up (history as a resource with a thermodynamic value). How to price each rule in the Metropolis energy so that heat counts only information that is actually unique.

The physics of how long things take to meet and relax when they diffuse on a lattice while tied together by strands. The repo's lattice is in effect a lattice-polymer Monte Carlo with reactions, and none of the twelve fields covers how its timing scales. Seminal sources: Verdier and Stockmayer (J. Chem. Phys. 1962), local moves on lattice chains; Rouse (1953) and de Gennes 'Reptation of a polymer chain' (1971), on how relaxation time grows with chain length, as N^2 to N^3; Carmesin and Kremer's bond-fluctuation method (Macromolecules 1988); Madras and Sokal 'Nonergodicity of local, length-conserving Monte Carlo algorithms for the self-avoiding walk' (J. Stat. Phys. 1987), where local moves cannot reach every state; Szabo, Schulten, Schulten (J. Chem. Phys. 1980), on how long a chain takes to loop its two ends together; Smoluchowski rates; Ovchinnikov and Zeldovich (1978) and Toussaint and Wilczek 'Particle-antiparticle annihilation in diffusive motion' (1983), where A+B annihilation slows to t^(-d/4) because the species separate into patches; Redner's 'A Guide to First-Passage Processes' (2001). Optional scaling bounds: Vitanyi 'Locality, communication and interconnect length in multicomputers' (SIAM J. Comput. 1988); Bilardi and Preparata 'Horizons of parallel computation' (1995); Frank's thesis 'Reversibility for Efficient Computing' (MIT 1999), the reversible 3D mesh. Focus: predict and fix the measured 10-12x slower backward runs, since undo pieces and un-copy twins have to meet again. Find out whether anti-trees and refund particles would stall from patch formation, and whether purely local strand moves can reach every state. Give expected costs in time and wire length for embedding post-S nets, whose wires are not spatially local, in a 3D lattice.

Dataflow and spatial hardware for fine-grained functional evaluation: the long engineering record on the trade between re-using a circuit and copying it under maximal parallelism. Seminal sources: Dennis and Misunas' static dataflow processor (ISCA 1975), one token per arc with code copied for each parallel instance; Arvind and Nikhil 'Executing a program on the MIT tagged-token dataflow architecture' (IEEE TC 1990) and Gurd, Kirkham, Watson 'The Manchester prototype dataflow computer' (CACM 1985), where code is re-entrant through context tags plus a matching store; Veen 'Dataflow machine architecture' (ACM Computing Surveys 1986); Culler and Arvind 'Resource requirements of dataflow programs' (ISCA 1988), with k-bounded loops that throttle runaway parallelism; Turner (1979) and Clarke et al. 'SKIM, the S, K, I reduction machine' (1980), combinator reduction in hardware; Budiu, Venkataramani, Chelcea, Goldstein 'Spatial computation' (ASPLOS 2004); Kung 'Why systolic architectures?' (1982); Carloni et al. on latency-insensitive design (2001) and Cortadella et al. on elastic circuits (2006). Focus: the tagged-token matching store is the hardware form of Abramsky's copy-tags, and it is exactly the global table keyed by ids that criterion 1 forbids. Static one-token-per-wire dataflow is local but must copy code. Lessons to carry over: measured parallelism profiles; throttling as a correctness condition, since too much unfolding deadlocks on resources; and ways to share a circuit locally without a global matching store.

Distributed algorithms that track copies, sharing and completion with a conserved quantity split on fork and recombined on join, instead of ids or a global view. Seminal sources: Dijkstra and Scholten 'Termination detection for diffusing computations' (IPL 1980), where each engaged node keeps a parent link and a deficit counter, a local history that collapses back as work finishes; Mattern 'Global quiescence detection based on credit distribution and recovery' (IPL 1989) and Huang's weight-throwing termination detection (ICDCS 1989); weighted reference counting (Bevan, PARLE 1987; Watson and Watson, PARLE 1987), where a copy splits a weight and a drop returns it, so the last holder knows it is last with no global count; Boyland 'Checking interference with fractional permissions' (SAS 2003) and Bornat, Calcagno, O'Hearn, Parkinson 'Permission accounting in separation logic' (POPL 2005), where splitting a whole permission gives shared read-only use and merging it back restores ownership. Focus: a local conservation law that witnesses 'these copies are twins' and 'all borrowers of this circuit are done', so that un-copy refunds and erasure heat are decided locally. A credit field on duplicators and wires as the lattice form of fuel. Fractional permissions as the type-level discipline for reading a circuit without consuming it, which is criterion 6's reuse instead of copying. Detecting that a maximally parallel net has finished with no central observer.
